B: Hiii! Hi, I'm Holly. Can you hear me okay?
A: I can, yeah. Gareth. How are you getting on?
B: Good, thanks! Third one, I'm getting into it now. Okay, I have to say, when I saw your photo I was like, he looks like a proper legend. You really remind me of my dad. Is that weird?
A: [laughs] No, I'll take that. Does your dad wear a fleece indoors and dry his socks on the radiator?
B: Literally, yes. Every winter. So what do you do?
A: I'm a countryside ranger, for the council in Darwen, up in Lancashire. Moors, woods, a reservoir walk. I look after the paths, run the volunteers, do the school visits. What about you?
B: I'm GM of a cocktail bar and restaurant in Chelmsford, so kind of the opposite of the moors. [laughs] Twenty-two staff, all the rotas, events, that sort of thing.
A: Twenty-two? Blimey. I've got two rangers and a rota of volunteers, and that's plenty some weeks.
B: Honestly, the staff are the best bit and the worst bit. I've got one lad at the minute who calls in sick every Saturday. Every Saturday. His nan's been ill about six times.
A: [laughs] Same nan every time?
B: That's what I said! What are your volunteers like, though? Do they turn up?
A: They're brilliant, mostly. A lot of them are retired. They'll be out in the rain at nine in the morning rebuilding a dry-stone wall, and they'll stop for a flask and argue about birds for half an hour. You've got to let them have the argument, mind, or they don't come back.
B: That's so nice. That's like my regulars, you've got to let them have their moan first, then you can sell them a bottle.
A: Same skill, really. You read the room. Sometimes it's a wet field, that's all.
B: Exactly that! Do you go out much yourself, like pubs and stuff?
A: Walking with a decent pub at the end, that's my idea of a weekend. Pint of real ale and a bit of a sit. I'm not much of a cocktail man, I'll be honest.
B: No, that's fine, I'm not judging. Okay, I'm a little bit judging. [laughs] What would you have if you had to?
A: Erm. Something that doesn't come with a sparkler in it?
B: I can work with that. I'd do you an old fashioned, proper one. It's basically a whisky with manners.
A: Whisky with manners. Go on, then, I'd try it.
B: See! I'm sorting out a hen do in Marbella at the minute, for my friend, and none of them want anything without a sparkler. It's chaos.
A: Marbella. I don't think I'd last a day. Me and Helen did the fjords in Norway for our twenty-fifth. That's more my sort of thing, mountains and a cold lake.
B: Oh, that's actually so romantic, though. Twenty-five years! That's goals.
A: She's put up with a lot. Choir every Tuesday, me out on the moors, the kitchen full of chilli on a Sunday. Our two have moved out now, so it's quiet.
B: Do you miss them?
A: Yeah. More than I let on, probably. Our lad's coming home for Sunday dinner this weekend, so, I'll be doing a hotpot. Anyway, what about you, how do you get on with the hours?
B: Honestly, not great. Me and Ryan sometimes go a couple of days just passing each other. I come in at two and he's asleep.
A: That's hard, that. You want to grab a night off and make him go walking with you.
B: He'd love that. He walks the dog more than me anyway. Do you know what, I might actually
